title: Remove-UnsafeCharacter is redundant with parameterization and corrupts stored data
description: Verified: Remove-UnsafeCharacter (podex.ps1:35-45) is a blacklist that doubles apostrophes and backslash-escapes " ; -- /* */ and backslash. It is applied to POST fields at post.ps1:43-46, but the INSERT is already parameterized (post.ps1:48-57). The sanitizer is therefore redundant AND corrupts legitimate data before storage: a note containing -- becomes \-\-, and O'Brien is stored as O''Brien. Blacklist input-mangling is the wrong model.
notes: Deleted the dead Remove-UnsafeCharacter blacklist from podex.ps1 (its only caller, api/crud/post.ps1, was already removed with the demo domain, so no writers invoke it). All pantry writes go through the parameterized DAL (New-PantryItem/Update-PantryItem bind @-params), so injection-shaped input is stored as data and user text is stored verbatim. Added two round-trip tests to tests/pantry.Tests.ps1 asserting values like O'Brien and 'batch -- "special"; C:\path\' round-trip byte-for-byte through create+read and update+read (no doubled apostrophes, no backslash-escaping). Replaced the function with a comment documenting why no pre-storage sanitizer exists. npm test -> 67 passed / 0 failed.
spec:
Detailed remediation steps:
1. Remove the Remove-UnsafeCharacter calls from post.ps1 (and any other writers); rely solely on parameterized queries to prevent injection.
2. Store user-supplied text verbatim so display is faithful.
3. Delete the Remove-UnsafeCharacter function from podex.ps1, or (if kept for some other purpose) rename it to a non-state-changing verb to satisfy PSScriptAnalyzer.
4. Add a test asserting a value like O'Brien -- note round-trips unchanged through create + read.
